items.title: ‘It’s been really a mess’: Meta insiders concerned over push to AI content moderation
items.summary: Several employees say rapid speed at which algorithms work means mistakes can happen at greater scale Meta employees have expressed concern at the company’s push to replace human moderators with artificial intelligence, claiming the technology is leading to mistakes with the potential for sweeping political consequences. The social media company, which owns Facebook and Instagram, has been experimenting with AI-driven moderation for years, first introducing it in 2017 to filter out violent extremist content. items.title: ‘Nature’s Ozempic’: oat sales soar as shoppers seek out foods that mimic effect of GLP-1s
items.summary: Porridge emerges as trend’s poster child with consumers looking to foods that help them feel full for longer, says Waitrose Sales of filling foods such as porridge oats that mimic the effect of taking weight-loss medication are booming on the back of social media hype billing them as “nature’s Ozempic” or “oatzempic”. items.title: Schumer accuses Huang of violating US export control laws amid shipments of chips to China
items.summary: Senate minority leader joins lawmakers from both parties outraged over Nvidia CEO’s reinstatement Chuck Schumer, the current Senate minority leader vying to lead the Democratic majority in the next Congress, accused Jensen Huang, the newly reinstated Nvidia CEO, of shipping “extremely advanced chips to China” and violating US export control laws. On Tuesday, Schumer said the move “amounts to the equivalent of selling rocket engines to the Soviets during the space race”. Continue reading...

items.title: Energy bills in Great Britain to rise 26% in January, lifting annual bills over £2,000
items.summary: Ofgem’s price cap will increase for third quarter in a row after rise in wholesale cost of gas Millions of British households will face annual energy bills of more than £2,000 a year for the first time since Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, as the cap on energy bills climbs for a third straight quarter. Gas and electricity prices will rise by 26% from January under the government’s new price cap after an increase in wholesale prices not experienced since the first winter after the invasion.
